changes_made.explanation: Removed redundant task entry and added output description. The paper focuses on controlled code-switching generation for NLP tasks.
Changed answer from No to Yes. The paper uses M-Index (Multilingual Index) and I-Index (Integration Index) as automatic metrics to evaluate code-switching patterns at the Intonation Unit level.
No LLMs are used as judges in this paper. LLMs are only mentioned in passing as examples of existing multilingual models.
No human evaluation is conducted in this paper. The evaluation is entirely based on automatic metrics applied to existing bilingual speech data.

overall_notes: This paper proposes new code-switching metrics using Intonation Units rather than word-level tokens. While it addresses NLG tasks (specifically controlled code-switching generation), it does not evaluate generated outputs in the traditional sense. Instead, it evaluates natural bilingual speech patterns to inform future NLG dataset construction. The automatic metrics used (M-Index and I-Index) are adapted from previous work but applied at the IU level for the first time.
